inputs.facts_req: Compared with reference runs of the stated fine-tune, this model shows a systematic tendency to over-specify: it invents concrete factual details, origins, dates, creators, measurements, backstories, and ontologies that neither reference gives, often on real-world entities and fictional/obscure ones alike. These additions are frequently dubious or wrong, sometimes contradict shared reference framing, and are often source-washed with official-sounding citations, URLs, named authorities, or bibliographic labels. It also more often literalizes cultural/symbolic claims, introduces cross-domain conflations, and occasionally mishandles requested footnote formats or uses awkward technical phrasing. The pattern is not just stylistic seed variation; it is a distinct propensity toward confident, citation-adorned hallucinated specificity in short document requests.
inputs.facts_docs: Compared with the reference runs, this model has a detectable continuation style: on raw passages it more readily leaves the shared continuation path, pivoting into new reader tasks, FAQ questions, comprehension prompts, or fresh story quests. It also often injects unsupported concrete specifics—dates, institutions, policy causes, infrastructure, ecological/scenic/product details—and sometimes frames them in polished promotional or skeptical-historiographic language. On practical/code prompts it tends to advance directly to implementation, validation steps, or broad INSTRUCT-style capability lists rather than staying in the references’ prose trajectory. These differences recur across detector-selected passages and appear larger than ordinary seed variation.

statement: Beyond what the described LoRA SFT run accounts for, this model shows a recurring behavioral signature: it confidently adds unsupported concrete details such as dates, origins, creators, measurements, institutions, causes, backstories, ontologies, and product/ecological/scenic specifics, often with official-sounding citations, URLs, authorities, or bibliographic labels. It does this across short document requests and raw continuations, including real, obscure, and fictional entities, and the additions are often dubious, wrong, or inconsistent with reference framing. It also more readily departs from passage-continuation trajectories into reader tasks, FAQs, comprehension prompts, story quests, implementation steps, validation plans, or broad instruction-style capability lists. These are concrete, repeated deviations from reference runs rather than mere stylistic seed variation.
